title: Private Pilot — midweek surge & kernel compatibility sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on a midweek egress surge that exposed a latency tail, discussion of kernel compatibility after last quantization patch, and planning for targeted benchmarks and a staged rollback window.
next_steps: Redwood SE to run full kernel compatibility sweep (quantized + fp16) and share results by 2027-04-12
HelixMed to export 24h of token-level trace for the surge window and upload to shared S3 link by 2027-04-09
Schedule a 1-hour maintenance window week of 2027-04-19 for optional kernel patch or rollback
Jordan to send updated pilot pricing showback for burst capacity by 2027-04-10
action_items: Priya Raman: run kernel compatibility test across quantized model fleet and attach perf matrix - due 2027-04-12
Sam Ortiz: collect and sanitize token-level traces for 2027-04-06 surge and upload to shared S3 - due 2027-04-09
Marcus Holt: prepare escalation note for enterprise support (SLA impact analysis) - due 2027-04-11
Eli Navarro: confirm KMS key rotation window constraints for any private deploy changes - due 2027-04-14
topics: midweek egress surge and tail latency
transcript:
Header: 2027-04-07 15:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Marcus (Redwood); Sam, Lena, Marta, Eli (HelixMed)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: ok everyone, thanks for jumping on, we had a pretty busy midweek so wanted to get a quick readout on the surge from Tuesday night. can you confirm you have the traces Sam?
[00:22] Sam Ortiz: yeah I pulled a quick set, there's like a three hour spike, roughly 21:10 to 00:15 UTC, I'm uploading sanitized traces to the S3 link now, maybe 10 minutes?
[00:38] Priya Raman: perfect, that's the window we suspect the kernel quantization change bumped a hot path—kv-cache misses plus slightly different kernel codegen for gelu. we saw similar in internal bench but not as pronounced.
[00:55] Marta Ruiz: just to add, our netops saw a small egress queue buildup on the VPC egress gateway. not full congestion but enough to nudge p99 up. could be combination of routing fanout we added last sprint.
[01:12] Dr. Lena Park: are we sure it's the kernel? I mean we pushed quantization last week and the model size reduced, but we also increased our throughput during a marketing campaign. correlation, not causation.
[01:30] Priya Raman: totally, that's why the compatibility sweep is key. two axes: kernel-level codegen differences and request-side shaping—are you running the same batching profile in prod as in staging?
[01:47] Sam Ortiz: prod had a burst config enabled, yes. staging is lower concurrency.
[02:03] Marcus Holt: quick note on observability — token-level traces show a rising ratio of prefix cache misses during the surge which matches our KV eviction threshold being reached. can we check the cache-config?
[02:18] Marta Ruiz: cache configured per-pod with 512MB, eviction at 80%. if many short-lived chat sessions start, eviction churn increases. we did see elevated short sessions around that time.
[02:34] Speaker 6: (murmur) mm-hmm
[02:45] Priya Raman: ok, action plan: I'll run the kernel compatibility sweep across your quantized variants and fp16 builds; that will show if any codegen path regresses latency at tail. also we'll replay your trace against a canary node to reproduce the egress profile.
[03:03] Sam Ortiz: do we have to do kernel rollback? what's risk?
[03:12] Jordan Lee: rollback is an option but we prefer targeted mitigation first: routing fallback to the previous kernel only for the canary region, adjust KV cache thresholds, and shape egress with a temporary QoS policy. rollback would be a last resort, requires KMS and HSM coordination for private deploys.
[03:34] Eli Navarro: speaking of KMS, any kernel change that touches agent binaries requires an audit entry and re-signing in our environment. we need to coordinate rotation windows.
[03:45] Priya Raman: noted. we'll keep binary digests and SLSA-compatible artifacts. Jordan, can you note that in the rollout plan?
[03:58] Jordan Lee: yes will include.
[04:05] Dr. Lena Park: what's the estimated impact on latency if we just tweak the cache thresholds? can we get p99 back down without touching kernels?
[04:18] Priya Raman: in internal sims, increasing cache to 768MB or lowering eviction to 90% cut p99 by about 15-20% for chatterty workloads. but memory footprint increases and might cause node pressure. need to test with your pod sizes.
[04:39] Sam Ortiz: we have headroom on our GPU nodes for memory, but the node driver has a pinned limit—we might need to tweak pod resource requests.
[04:50] Marcus Holt: also worth noting that routing fanout contributed. we can reduce model fanout during the surge window via a temporary route policy—less parallelization, shorter tail but potentially higher aggregate CPU for those requests. tradeoff.
[05:07] Jordan Lee: tradeoff call: lower fanout + higher cache often helps tail without kernel changes. we should benchmark both.
[05:18] Marta Ruiz: are you able to run the benchmark in our staging or you need trace replay?
[05:25] Priya Raman: replay is ideal; we'll run both replay and synthetic high-concurrency tests. Sam, thanks for uploading the traces.
[05:33] Sam Ortiz: uploading now (background noise).
[05:40] Jordan Lee: small tangent—Marcus, did the telemetry show any region-specific failover?
[05:47] Marcus Holt: yes, our traces show a modest uptick in fallback routing to the eu-west cluster when the us-east egress gateway hit queueing. the fallback worked but increased cross-region latency. worth discussing fallback thresholds.
[06:04] Dr. Lena Park: cross-region latency is a big no for us for some flows due to PHI. we need stricter gating.
[06:13] Eli Navarro: correct — cross-region fallback must be opt-in per route; we currently have some default fallbacks enabled. need to ensure PHI flows are pinned.
[06:24] Jordan Lee: we'll add route tags and explicit pinning for PHI. Priya, can you look at route policy rules and propose a pinning config?
[06:32] Priya Raman: yes, will propose via doc.
[06:35] [10:02] Sam Ortiz: question on the kernel compatibility sweep—how long will it take?
[10:09] Priya Raman: estimate 3 business days to run across all quantized variants for your fleet size, less if we parallelize. results will include perf matrix and any regressions.
[10:18] Marcus Holt: also, I want to remind everyone about the SLA escalation path. if p99 remains over threshold for more than 2 hours during a production event, we'll escalate to Level 2 and open a support war room.
[10:30] Dr. Lena Park: understood. we want the war room but prefer preemptive mitigations.
[10:36] Jordan Lee: ok on war room. next, maintenance window—we discussed possible rollback week of 2027-04-19. is that acceptable?
[10:47] Sam Ortiz: yes that week is fine, prefer weekend window.
[10:50] Eli Navarro: weekend is preferable for KMS rotation. will check dates and constraints.
[11:00] Priya Raman: security note: any rollback needs signed artifacts and an audit trail; Marcus, can you own the rollback runbook draft?
[11:09] Marcus Holt: yep will draft and share by next Tuesday.
[11:16] Jordan Lee: quick pricing note — Jordan: we'll send an updated showback for burst capacity; with the surge profile we can propose a short-term burst add-on at negotiated rate to avoid throttling.
[11:28] Dr. Lena Park: please include cost impact per 10k tokens at p99 delta.
[11:34] Jordan Lee: will do.
[11:40] [48:12] Marta Ruiz: last item — can Redwood provide a lightweight fallback runbook we can use for on-call? a single page with commands and escalation contacts.
[48:25] Priya Raman: yes we'll produce a one-pager and include snippet for route policy toggles, KV cache tuning knobs, and rollback steps.
[48:36] Jordan Lee: ok wrap — recap: Priya runs kernel sweep; Sam uploads traces; Marcus drafts rollback runbook; Eli confirms KMS windows; Jordan sends pricing and rollout plan.
[48:55] Sam Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread.
[49:05] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, talk soon.

Notes: transcription imperfect — occasional label mismatches, filler words. references: shared S3 link (internal), kernel-sweep doc (PRD link), one-pager fallback-runbook (to be produced).
